title: kbmon --events orders committed ops rows of one millisecond by row id, not write order
goal: kbmon --events reads committed ops rows of one millisecond in their write order (mon_events passes the clone root to mon_log.in_spool_order), so a landing whose land.step shares a millisecond with its land.end keeps its step span

run:
import json, os, sys, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
home = tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.environ["CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA"] = home
os.environ["CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT"] = os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
d = Path(home) / "kb" / "_querylog" / "ops" / "2026-10"
d.mkdir(parents=True)
ts = "2026-10-19T10:00:00.123Z"
rows = [{"run": "r", "counts": {"rows": 2}},
        {"id": "zz-late-id", "ts": ts, "event": "land.step", "item": "BG-testtest", "step": "verify", "exit": 0, "ms": 5},
        {"id": "aa-early-id", "ts": ts, "event": "land.end", "item": "BG-testtest", "exit": 0, "ms": 9, "lane": "main"}]
(d / "20261019T100000Z-aaaaaaaa.jsonl").write_text("\n".join(json.dumps(r) for r in rows) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
import mon_events


class Ctx:
    root = home


spans = mon_events.ops_records(Ctx, 0)[1]
print(len(spans), "spans")
sys.exit(0 if any(s.get("name") == "kb.land.step" for s in spans) else 1)
